newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello notes favourable rate cut comments.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello notes favourable rate cut comments.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello told ruling parties members of parliament that following price data last week, commentators saw conditions favourable for the prospect of lower interest rates, a party spokesman said on Tuesday.

"He said there had been speculation about cuts in rates, he reaffirmed that's a matter for the Reserve Bank to take decisions about," the party spokesman told reporters, reporting on today's regular meeting of government parliamentarians.

"He said that there had been a focus on two indicators, firstly that the CPI (consumer price index) is now at pre-Whitlam inflation rates and secondly that weekly ordinary time earnings, were the second indicators that had been looked at," he said.
"So he said that there were good conditions for further prospects in that regard," the spokesman said.
However, the spokesman repeatedly emphasised that Costello had been describing the favourable interest rate outlook seen by commentators, not by himself.

Figures released last week showed annual wages growth had fallen to 3.5 percent in August from 3.7 percent in May and that annual headline inflation had fallen to 2.1 percent in the September quarter, its lowest level for two years.
Underlying inflation was 2.4 percent in the September quarter, comapred to a 3.1 percent rise in the year to June 30.
